summary: Thistledew, a 100-foot CCC-built state tower in Itasca County, was sold and may have gone to Wisconsin; no source describes the hilltop today.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor stairway tower, state tower number 33
facts.status_note: Gone from its Itasca County hilltop; a county list says it may now be in Wisconsin, which is not confirmed

events.note: Erected by the Civilian Conservation Corps, per the county list
1959 survey notes: four-legged steel structure with an observation room; overall height 125 feet
Survey note says the station was destroyed; the list does not say whether the tower was already gone

evidence.supports: 100-foot Aermotor stairway tower erected by the CCC in 1937
evidence.quote: Thistledew was a 100 foot Aermotor stairway tower erected by the CCC in 1937.

evidence.supports: stood on a hill at the north end of Thistledew Lake
evidence.quote: Thistledew stood on a hill at the north end of Thistledew Lake.

evidence.supports: Mn MFS owner, 1937, 100 ft stair tower
1959 survey: four-legged steel structure with an observation room
evidence.quote: Survey notes from 1959: It is a four legged steel structure with an observation room at the top.

evidence.supports: overall height 125 feet; 2001 note says station destroyed
tower purchased, changed hands, may be in Wisconsin
evidence.quote: The tower was purchased, changed hands and may be in Wisconsin now.

evidence.supports: FFLA list shows Thistledew at the Itasca site as Tower Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1959 survey note gives an overall height of 125 feet, while the list's table and history give the tower as 100 feet; the story gives both, as the list does for other towers.

notes_for_editor: All of the history comes from one county list (Tlkremer, Wikimedia Commons). The 1959 survey note, its 125-foot height and the 2001 'Station is destroyed' line sit in the same notes cell as the Thistledew description in the PDF text (re-read 2026-10-21; the cell follows the Third River entry), so the attribution rests on that layout rather than an explicit label. The Wisconsin move is unconfirmed and the list does not date the sale. No source describes the hilltop today. The unsourced visit.climbable flag was removed from facts on the fact-check pass. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 5 page reads.
